Use case: illustration-story. Generate ONE new Nightglass comic panel, square composition, no text, no lettering, no balloons. Reference 1 supplies original thin controlled anime drawing, elegant face proportions, inhabited navy/cyan city with selective amber windows. Reference 2 supplies stable cast construction ONLY: Aren is slim adult dark-haired man in long-sleeved ivory waist jacket, black high-neck shirt/trousers/gloves, red courier cord; Pell older gray-haired stubbled man in mustard work jacket. Exclude the sheet's tall rig, spear, ray and extra people. Reference 3 is CURRENT STATE/geography control only, not visual style. Reference 4 if supplied is the preceding selected panel: preserve its identities and current physical geography, but advance exactly the new action/state below. Use expressive attractive acting, clear hands, broad quiet surface shapes, matte stone, no microtexture everywhere. Scene: old postal stair, blue night, warm windows distant. Aren steps off the upper stair toward the landing THREE metres down-right. One thin cyan line runs from the pommel ring behind his RIGHT fist to the BLACK metal post on that lower landing. Sword points left, away from the line. Empty left arm balances; boots airborne.
Current state authoritative: Envelope hidden chest; one taut pommel-to-post line; torn hem; left sleeve intact; Pell remains upper stair.
Camera: wide side showing whole human and both endpoints. Keep quiet dark upper 20 percent for later dialogue. One black envelope only, in the stated location; cream wallet concealed; do not add objects from sheet. No future damage or characters. One frozen moment. Make visible causal hand/contact/endpoint information clear.

inspection: Readable airborne descent. Sword now RIGHT and line leaves rear pommel, runs partly behind body to single lower post; sleeves intact, envelope hidden. Old hem tear not clearly retained. Wet-looking stone departs matte target but secondary. Adjacent method did not preserve original hand mistake here; ownership changes across sequence.
